initial_broad_formulation.reason: Activation, guard, UI justification, first/third-party attribution, top-level-function responsibility and dependency reachability are already substantially covered by AppContext, FlowCog, AppIntent, AsDroid, AutoPPG, LibRadar/LibScout/MAPS and supply-chain reachability work.

reformulated_hypothesis: For multiple first-party contexts that converge on the same shared third-party sensitive Host, treat each nearest first-party-to-third-party call-boundary instance as a separate responsibility unit, preserve its first-party orchestrator/activation/guard/UI/Role/distance context, exclude library identity and raw size, and test whether this instance-level deconvolution supplies abstaining bidirectional marginal evidence for a frozen Stage-I bounded correction.
decision_basis: No checked primary paper was found that simultaneously uses the same shared third-party sensitive Host as a convergence point, deconvolves it by nearest ownership-boundary instance, preserves first-party orchestration context per instance, and applies the evidence to selective bounded correction.
The surviving distinction is the responsibility unit and deconvolution operation, not the use of activation, guard, UI, ownership, attention or weak supervision by themselves.
The hypothesis has explicit falsification gates: multi-boundary coverage, exact alignment, identity-zero controls, degree-preserving shuffles, side-specific direction signal and broken control.
